left.title: GOP running out of options on Trump’s border emergency
left.body: Senate Republicans are unlikely to be permitted to dramatically amend the House-passed resolution that would overturn the president’s national emergency, suggesting they will be confronted with a simple referendum on the president’s controversial declaration later this week.
left.roundup: Senate Republicans are reportedly working on a compromise that would limit presidential powers to declare national emergencies while also ensuring that the Senate approves President Trump's declaration for $3.6 billion in border wall funding.

center.title: Senate rejection of Trump border emergency no longer certain
center.body: The White House and Republican senators sought compromise Tuesday on limiting presidents’ powers to unilaterally declare national emergencies, as chances improved that President Donald Trump might avoid a long-expected rejection by Congress of his effort to divert billions more for building barriers along the Mexican border. As a Thursday showdown vote in the Senate neared, GOP Sens. Mike Lee of Utah, Thom Tillis of North Carolina and others were talking with the White House about related legislation that would curb the ability of presidents to declare future emergencies. right.title: GOP looking to curtail Trump's emergency powers
right.body: Senate Republicans said Tuesday they are looking to "revisit" a law that allows presidents to use the National Emergencies Act to redirect federal funding, as President Trump is proposing to do to build a southern border wall. The GOP hopes a promise to take up legislation reining in the president will keep fewer Republicans from voting with Democrats this week on a resolution to revoke Trump’s border emergency.
